source_text: Λοιπὸν ὁ παντεπόπτης θεὸς καὶ δεσπότης τῶν πνευμάτων καὶ κύριος πάσης σαρκός, ό ἐκλεξάμενος τὸν κύριον Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν καὶ ἡμᾶς δἰ αὐτοῦ εἰς λαὸν περιούσιον, δῴη πάσῃ ψυχῇ ἐπικεκλημένῃ τὸ μεγαλοπρεπὲς καὶ ἅγιον ὄνομα αὐτοῦ πίστιν, φόβον, εἰρήνην, ὑπομονὴν καὶ μακροθυμίαν, ἐγκράτειαν, ἁγνείαν, σωφροσύνην, εἰς εὐαρέστησιν τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ διὰ τοῦ ἀρχιερέως καὶ προστάτου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, δἰ οὗ αὐτῷ δόξα καὶ μεγαλωσύνη, κράτος καὶ τιμή, καὶ νῦν καὶ εἰς πάντας τοῦς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων ἀμήν.
orientation: Clement, writing from the Roman church, closes the letter with a prayer that God grant every soul called by his name the virtues needed to please him through Christ.
pass_a_gloss: For the rest, the All-Seeing God and Master of the spirits and Lord of all flesh, the [one] having chosen the Lord Jesus Christ and us through him for a people [as his] own possession, may he give to every soul [that] has been called by the magnificent and holy name of him faith, fear, peace, endurance and patience, self-control, purity, sound-mindedness, for pleasing to the name of him through the high priest and protector of us Jesus Christ, through whom to him [be] glory and majesty, might and honor, both now and into all the ages of the ages. Amen.

choices.why: Marks the transition to the closing prayer; 'for the rest' is too literal and archaic.
Keeps the genitive plural force and the title's solemnity; 'spirits' matches the source exactly.

choices.english: a people of his own possession
choices.why: Renders the biblical idiom for God's special people; 'possession' preserves the sense of belonging.

choices.term: ἐπικεκλημένῃ τὸ μεγαλοπρεπὲς καὶ ἅγιον ὄνομα αὐτοῦ
choices.english: that has been called by his magnificent and holy name
choices.why: The dative participle is passive; 'called by' captures that the name is the agent of calling.
rejected: that has invoked his magnificent and holy name
named with his magnificent and holy name

choices.english: so that they may please his name
choices.why: The purpose clause is rendered naturally; 'pleasing' as a noun is awkward in English.
rejected: for the pleasing of his name

choices.term: εἰς πάντας τοῦς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων
choices.why: Standard English doxological formula for the Greek idiom 'unto all the ages of the ages'.
rejected: unto all the ages of the ages
for all the ages of ages

bible_refs.note: δεσπότης τῶν πνευμάτων καὶ κύριος πάσης σαρκός

pass_b_english: Finally, may the All-Seeing God, the Master of the spirits and Lord of all flesh, grant to every soul that has called upon his magnificent and holy name faith, fear, peace, endurance, patience, self-control, purity, and sound-mindedness, so that they may please his name through our high priest and protector Jesus Christ.
He chose the Lord Jesus Christ, and through Christ he chose us to be a people of his own possession.
Through Christ be glory and majesty, might and honor to God, both now and for ever and ever. Amen.

polish.changed: Broke the long opening sentence into shorter, clearer statements, identified God as the subject of the final doxology, and kept every petition and title intact.
Split the long petition into four short paragraphs, clarified that 'he' refers to God, and kept the closing doxology as its own sentence.

Merged the fragmented sentences into a single flowing prayer, kept 'Master' and 'Lord' consistently for God, clarified that the gifts are granted so that the called souls may please God's name, and preserved every petition and doxology exactly.

notes.why: Frequent switching between 'Master' and 'Lord' for God may seem intentional but lacks consistency.
notes.fix: Standardize divine titles or explain the variation.

problems.quote: called by his magnificent and holy name
problems.source_quote: ἐπικεκλημένῃ τὸ μεγαλοπρεπὲς καὶ ἅγιον ὄνομα αὐτοῦ
problems.why: Perfect middle with accusative: the soul has called upon the name, not been called by it.
problems.fix: to every soul that has called upon his magnificent and holy name
problems.ruling: ἐπικεκλημένῃ is perfect middle/passive with accusative τὸ ὄνομα: 'having invoked/called upon his name' (1 Clem 64). 'Called by his name' reverses agency; soul invokes the name.

edits.old: to every soul called by his magnificent and holy name
edits.new: to every soul that has called upon his magnificent and holy name

fixed: fixed agency: changed to 'has called upon' — ἐπικεκλημένῃ with accusative τὸ μεγαλοπρεπὲς καὶ ἅγιον ὄνομα αὐτοῦ means the soul has invoked/called upon the name, not been called by it
